correctness.rationale: The geometric smoothness criterion follows by applying the gradient equations on the three coordinate lines and then to the three nonzero squared coordinates. In the latter case the coefficient matrix has diagonal 2 and off-diagonal r,s,t, determinant 2(4+rst-r²-s²-t²); if the three principal 2x2 minors are nonzero, a nonzero radical vector must have all entries nonzero. Even exponents force the canonical Hasse–Witt matrix to be diagonal, and the diagonal entries are independently identified by the quartic elliptic-quotient coefficient B²+2AC. The degree-eight quotient isogeny identifies 5-primary invariants, so rank counts nonzero entries and a=3-f. On the smooth simultaneous-zero locus the differences force equal squares; the common parameter with even sign changes solves (a-2)²(a²-2a-2)=0. The excluded root is singular, and the irreducible quadratic has two distinct smooth roots in F25, neither the negative of the other, giving eight ordered triples. A separate exact enumeration gave rank vectors (8,96,1110,10469) over F25 and (0,12,0,11) over F5, with 11683 and 23 smooth triples, respectively; the geometric classification is symbolic.
residual_risks: The finite census is for normalized ordered coefficient triples; it is not a moduli-class count or on its own a proof over the algebraic closure.
